content.content:
- F-363 **A superscript follows a dotted access and a parenthesised call on both paths.** `p.wq^T`, `B.n^2`, `B.f()^T` and `B.data[5]^2` parse as the operator applied to the whole dotted primary to its left, and `(f(x))^T`, `(f(x))!` and `(a^b)!` run under walk as they do compiled; `f(x)^T` and `f(x)^2` stay a static error on both paths (walk: "the argument should not be immediately followed by a non-expression element"; the checker: "Item at this location must be an expression, not an operator."). The parser reads a primary with a dot as the front of the math items that follow it (`parser/Expression.rats:386-400`), so a subscript, a parenthesised item or a tight identifier after a dotted method call parses too; of these, one test compiles a subscript, `Maker.f()[5]^2` (`compiler_tests/SubscriptThenSuperscriptCompiled`). The one node kind that the parser builds for a single item is the one the parenthesised spelling built, so neither the checker nor the code generator changed. Walk's postfix branch evaluates an operand in parentheses as one expression (`interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:965-970`). So a model line may write `p.wq^T x` and `(onehot(ks, 5))^T dx`; a selector after a superscript, `B.data^T.v`, is still a syntax error, and a superscript after a subscript that is a math item of its own, `x[5]^2` or `B.f()[5]^2`, compiles (F-387) and fails under walk (row 1); in `B.data[5]^2` the subscript is part of the dotted primary. Tests: `tests/SuperscriptAfterDottedAccess.fss`, `tests/SuperscriptAfterParenthesisedCall.fss`, `tests/SuperscriptAfterCallRefused.fss` with its `.test`, and `compiler_tests/SuperscriptAfterDottedAccessCompiled.test`, `SuperscriptAfterParenthesisedCallCompiled.test`, `XXXSuperscriptAfterCallRefusedCompiled.test`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-superscript-after/REPORT.md`, "Each form on the base and after" and "The trees".

- F-369 **A top-level tuple binding compiles: each name is a top-level variable of its element's type, and the right side is evaluated once, at the first read of any name.** The checker gives the tuple that it rebuilds from the checked elements their tuple type, from which each name's thunk reads its own (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Decls.scala:272-277`); where only some names declare a type and the right side is no tuple expression of as many elements, it checks the right side again against each name's type (`Decls.scala:324-336`). The code generator keeps the right side's value in a hidden class `<Component>$tuple$<first name>` and gives each name its own class, whose initializer takes its element out by the tuple's typed getter (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:6908`); a wildcard binds nothing. Every compiled top-level variable is initialized at its first read, not at load as under walk, so a binding of wildcards alone never evaluates its right side (row 1011). So a model line of this form compiles as written, the model's lines 17 to 19 among them, and a name bound so is typed as a single binding's is: `explorations/run-c4/src/MicroGptFlat.fss:72`, `beta1 m`, is a new checker site against the one library (F-58). Under walk the same right side runs once for each name and once more (row 1026). The checker checks a local tuple binding's declared names beside untyped names in the same way (row 1029, fixed; `compiler_tests/LocalTupleBindingMixedTypes`, `XXXLocalTupleBindingMixedRefused`), and a typed tuple binding over an `if` with tuple branches compiles (row 1031, fixed). Tests: `compiler_tests/TopLevelTupleBindingCompiled.test`, `TopLevelTupleBindingImport.test`, `TopLevelTupleBindingMixedTypes.test`, `XXXTopLevelTupleBindingType.test`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-tuple-binding/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why" and "The binding as compiled".

- F-387 **The compiled path compiles a primary whose math items all apply in turn to its front: `x[5]^2` is `(x[5])^2` and `g[1][2]` is `(g[1])[2]`; and a subscript as a math item before a tightly juxtaposed item: `x[5]k` is `(x[5]) k`.** The checker checks the one application that the reassociation leaves, at the expected type, and writes each subscript as a call of the subscript operator's method, as the desugaring before it writes every other subscript (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Operators.scala`). Walk still fails on these forms (row 1), so a program for both paths writes `(x[5])^2`. Test: `compiler_tests/SubscriptThenSuperscriptCompiled.test`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-small-gaps/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why", item 2.

content.content: - F-372 **The code generator writes each inherited method once into a trait's or an object's class, runs the declaration of the lowest type that declares it, and forwards to a body that an imported api's trait holds.** For the class of a trait or an object the code generator leaves out each declaration whose method a type strictly below the declaring type declares again at the same parameter types, self apart. A dispatch method's gathering still compares declarations as schemas over each trait's own bounds, not at the instance. So the choice is a relation between two declarations, not the order of the gathered methods, and the library's shape of P-47, `MAX` in `StandardMinMax`, `StandardTotalOrder` and a type below, does not stop a class at load (row 990, fixed). A method that an imported api's trait declares without `abstract` counts as a body in that trait's class, so a trait that is not first in an extends clause gives its body, plain, generic and functional methods alike (row 732, fixed). The batch's planner chose both readings as defaults, and the curator has not decided them; by the traits chapter's text, an object that reaches one method along two paths, one through a trait that declares it again, inherits both declarations, and the checker refuses that form where the traits are self-typed and generic (row 1037). A functional method with self not first is written once, not again beside the dispatch method of the same name (row 571, fixed), so such a class loads; but an object's dispatch method still tests the receiver in place of the argument, and where the receiver itself has the own declaration's parameter type, a call answers wrongly with no error: with `object Pq extends { K, P }` declaring `mark(x: K, self)` beside `P`'s `mark(x: Any, self)`, `mark(1, Pq)` gives 3 where walk gives 1 (rows 1038 and 573). Tests: `compiler_tests/TraitOwnMethodBesideInheritedCompiled`, `ApiTraitMethodNotFirstCompiled`, `TraitMethodDiamondRedeclaredCompiled`, `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-method-forwarders/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why".

content.content:
6367:\seclabel{revival-supported}
as a comment: ``(perhaps with additional modification and evolution of their
design)''.
The sentence of the introduction stood under a draft note of its own section
that says that keyword and varargs parameters are not yet supported.
A reversal would restore the three passages below.
The state of each item, with the rows of the revival's gap ledger, is in note
6 of
\nolinkurl{explorations/coordinator/tools/spec-html/answers-2026-11-15.md},
and who built each part is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/reviews/preface-list-provenance-2026-11-16.md}, in the
revival's repository.
\item[Effect] The list names what the implementation lacks.
The limits that it names are these, by the rows of the revival's gap ledger.
The interpreter makes binary calls of an operator repeated between three or
more operands (row~29).
The interpreter skips the coverage check for a generic object (row~665), and
departs on two generic functional methods of one type (rows~779 and~780).
Keyword parameters are built in neither implementation (row~652).
The code generator refuses a varargs parameter under the compiled path's own
library, which declares no \TYP{ImmutableArray}; against \library\ it compiles
one, and a program compiled against \library\ can run, as one that prints a
line of text does, but not one that calls a declaration with a varargs parameter,
since the class of the array of its arguments does not load (row~1091);
\secref{revival-varargs} names the forms that it does not yet compile.
An object takes no varargs parameter (row~11).
Nothing checks \KWD{io}, and nothing reads \KWD{atomic} on a function.
An underscore before a digit is read as a radix (row~15).
Of the static parameters that are not types, \KWD{nat} and \KWD{int} are
built; \KWD{bool} is not usable (rows~307 and~761), and a compiled generic
object with an \KWD{opr} parameter fails when it runs (row~366).
A function with the modifier \KWD{test} runs; a test with generators and a
property stop their component (rows~121 and~122).
Three forms of \KWD{where} clauses are built (\secref{revival-where},
\secref{revival-conditional}); the implementations apply a conditional
extension where its condition fails (row~774), and compiled code checks no
\KWD{where} clause.
An abstract function declaration works in a trait, not at the top level.
The interpreter runs a function's contract; the code generator refuses a
function with one (row~701), and both implementations drop the contract of a
trait or an object (row~781).

\begin{itemize}

\item generic overloading check of two functional methods of one type under
the interpreter
\item definite assignment check
\item keyword parameters; varargs parameters in compiled code and in the
parameters of an object
\item varargs expressions
\item some modifiers (\KWD{override} in compiled code, \KWD{io},
\KWD{atomic} on a function, ...)
\item qualified names
\item identifiers in which a digit follows an underscore
\item ASCII conversion other than of names
\item Unicode canonicalization
\item array comprehensions
\item reduction variables
\item object copy
\item unboxed types
\item mutual recursion in value objects
\item thread fairness guarantee
\item distributions
\item matrix unpasting

content.content:
- F-373 **The compiled path runs `label` and `exit`: an exit is a thrown `LabelExit` that names one evaluation of its label block, and reaches it from a loop's body and from another task.** `CodeGen.forLabel` makes a new target for each evaluation of the block and takes, in a handler, the exits that name it; `CodeGen.forExit` throws `LabelExit.of(value, target)` (`runtimeSystem/LabelExit.java`). A function expression or a task whose body exits captures the target as it captures any immutable variable. A group of forked arms joins the arms that it forked before the exit passes it: at four threads every forked iteration of a parallel `for` runs to its end or to its own exit, and the label's value is the exit of the first arm in the arms' order; at one thread the iterations after the exit do not run. No `catch` clause takes an exit. So the one library's `Indexed.indexOf` compiles in its own form (the test's `Holder.indexOf`), and row 81 is fixed. Three of the compiled answers were chosen as the path was built, and the curator has not decided them; walk answers each otherwise: which evaluation an exit leaves where the block is evaluated again inside itself, compiled the one in which the exit's function was made (row 1042); whether a `catch` of `Exception` takes an exit, compiled no (row 1040); and what an exit is after its label block has completed, compiled an uncaught `LabelExit` that ends the program (row 1041). Four limits stand, each with its test: an exit out of an `atomic` block loses the block's writes (row 1039); a `finally` clause on the exit's way does not run (row 890); a label block as a call's later argument fails verification (row 322); a label block whose value joins a numeral with a number stops the code generator (row 340), though by P-50 the numeral takes the label's expected type; a program binds the numeral to a typed variable first. Test: `compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled`, which fails with 'Can't compile Label' without `forLabel` and `forExit`. A commit that fails runs the block again, as at a normal end, and an exception other than an exit still discards the writes. A nested block's commit hands its writes to the outer one, whose commit on the same exit stores them. Neither path tells an exit to an enclosing label from one to a completed label block, so the latter commits the blocks it passes too (row 1041). Under walk an exit or an exception out of a `tryatomic` block that no `atomic` block encloses is wrapped in a `RuntimeException` and reaches neither its label nor a `catch` (rows 1110 and 1111). So a program may exit out of an atomic block (`Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:59-63`). Tests: `tests/ExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss`, `compiler_tests/ExitOutOfAtomicCompiled`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-exit-out-of-atomic/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why" and "The tests: failing on the base, passing after".
EOF

content.content:
not block it; a row keeps its own cells. With
                             --check it writes nothing: it prints whether
                             TEXT fits, and the characters that the notes
                             (700) and the row (1,200) would have left with
                             it and have left now; exit 0 if it fits, 1 if
                             not, so a note is sized before it is written
  rewrite N FILE             FILE holds row N's whole new line (its # cell N
                             or ?, or the seven cells after it); checks it
                             against the template and writes it in the row's
                             place, its earlier line in the history
                             ("rewritten"): the route that corrects a claim,
                             cuts notes, or moves a reproducer. A FIXED or
                             DUPLICATE row stays so (a FIXED row's commit is
                             checked); a row becomes one only by close or
                             duplicate
  close N --commit HASH --test NAME [--settled TEXT] [--note TEXT] [--claim C]
        [--class C] [--spec C] [--found-by C]
                             after the fix has landed: HASH must be in HEAD's
                             history; NAME a test under the test folders, a
                             file under explorations/coordinator/tools/ (a
                             tool's own test), or none, which needs --note
                             with the reason; a CONTESTED row needs --settled
                             naming what settled its question (the curator's
                             answer, a POSITIONS entry), and only it takes
                             it; writes the one-line FIXED row (the claim's
                             first sentence, the test or none as reproducer,
                             notes `fixed HASH[; settled by TEXT][; TEXT];
                             full text: history, row N`); the options give
                             cells the old row lacks in the template's form
  duplicate N --of M [--add TEXT] [--claim C] [--class C] [--spec C]
        [--reproducer C] [--found-by C]
                             makes row N a DUPLICATE pointer to row M (notes
                             `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`);
                             --add appends TEXT to row M's notes
  check [--rows FILE] [--base COMMIT] [--summary]
                             lints every row against the template, and the
                             tables' headers, numbers and order; --rows lints
                             a file holding only row lines instead; --base
                             also checks that every row at COMMIT is the same
                             line now or has its full earlier line in the
                             history file, and that the set of row numbers is
                             unchanged; --summary prints only the counts by
                             rule; exit 1 on any failure
  landing-check BASE [--head REV] [--facts FILE] [--positions FILE]
                             the checks of a landing that need no reading
                             (ledger-health-2026-10-22/REPORT.md, 6.3), on the
                             ledger and on BASE..REV (REV default HEAD), one
                             line per finding, exit 1 on any:
                               template  check with no allowance, and check
                                 --base BASE (new rows allowed, none gone)
                               xxx-gone  each XXX test of the test folders

explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh
#!/bin/bash
# junit.sh <label> <dir-of-tests> <Name.test>... : the gather of climb batch N runs each .test through the
# harness in the main tree (fortress junit, the compiled test harness, as climb batch 6.5's gather ran its pair),
# in the order given, so that a link test runs before its XXX run test. Each named component's cache entries are
# removed before the list and after it. First line: the machine line (protocol.md, principle 2).
# ONE_JVM=1 (added 2026-09-29 for the repair on the merged tree, coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md, "A repair
# of tests and records only"): the whole list in one fortress junit run, one JVM, as the gate's track runs them
# together; Shell junit hands the list to FileTests.suiteFromListOfFiles (Shell.java:1086), which puts its
# compile and link tests before its run tests (FileTests.java:997-1004), so a link test still runs first.
# The environment is env.sh's, set here without sourcing it, since env.sh also removes parser directories in
# /tmp. The tree is the one this script is in. FORTRESS_THREADS=4 is the pin of build.xml's fastTrack macro,
# which runs the gate's compiled tracks. The JVMs keep their temporary files, parser directories among them,
# in the tree's tmp/.
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export FORTRESS_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.." && pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=4
mkdir -p "$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
FH=$FORTRESS_HOME; L=${1:?label}; D=$(cd "${2:?dir}" && pwd); shift 2
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress"
CP=$(../bin/fortress_classpath | tail -1)
echo "# junit.sh $L $(date -u +%FT%TZ); nproc $(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=$FORTRESS_THREADS; tree $(git -C $FH rev-parse --short HEAD)$(git -C $FH diff --quiet HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library || echo ' with the next rung applied, not yet committed'); tests from $D"
clean () { for t in "$@"; do n=$(sed -n 's/^tests=//p' "$D/$t" | head -1); [ -n "$n" ] && find ../default_repository/caches -name "*$n*" -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null; done; }
clean "$@"
if [ -n "${ONE_JVM:-}" ]; then
  files=(); for t in "$@"; do files+=("$D/$t"); done
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit, one JVM: $*"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "${files[@]}" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240

Climb batch 35, rung W: walk now applies a subscript that is a math item with all its indices (`x[5]^2`, `m[3,7]^2`, `g[3][7]`, `x[5]k`) and runs a tuple binding's right side once, at the top level and as an object's field (rows 1 and 1026 close; row 152's notes rewritten); `ant testSystem` 881, 0 failures; no stage moves.
== self-not-first-dispatch
Climb batch 35, rung S (self not first): the dispatch method of a trait's or an object's functional method reads each argument at its own local (`OverloadSet.argumentLocal`, overridden in `ForTraitOrObject`), so rows 573 and 1038 close with their three tests promoted (`FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast`, with a trait case, `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested`) and a self-second-of-three case added to `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst`; the 46 functional method tests of the compiler track pass in one JVM; row 594's test still fails at its own site; no stage run, by the brief.

Climb batch 35 rung A (`wip/rung-exit-out-of-atomic`, `eb2f652487`, `8bd7cfcf0a`): an exit out of an atomic block commits the block's transaction on both paths (a failed commit runs the block again; an exception still discards), row 1039 closes with its two tests promoted; NEW-A-1 opens, walk's exit out of `tryatomic` lost in a `RuntimeException`, with its `XXX` test; row 1041 gains the consequence that such an exit commits the blocks it passes, for item 562.
